title: Direct quotient normalization and the concrete sections adjunction
statement: For X, A, J and U as in [def-sfb-adic-perfect-module-functors], let q_n be the constant quotient map restricted to U and let L_A and S_A be the constant realization and sections functors of [def-sfb-adic-perfect-slice-sections]. Define quotientRealization_n=L_A followed by change(q_n), and rawRightAdjoint_n=res(q_n) followed by S_A. Construct quotientRealization_n left adjoint rawRightAdjoint_n. Reassociate scalar extension, commute it with restriction to U and apply the completion cone equation to construct an isomorphism from the actual completed quotient realization F_n to quotientRealization_n. Transport the adjunction to obtain a proved Nonempty(F_n left adjoint rawRightAdjoint_n), and select rawAdjunction from this proved theorem. No unproved existence result selects data.

proof.text: Use localAdjunction and the slice/sections comparison maps already constructed for an arbitrary small site.

Use the proved scalar/slice comparisons and constantPresentationIso from AdicPerfectModelCompleteReduction. Reassociate the two scalar changes with adicFiniteChangeComp and the completion cone equation coefficientMap followed by projection equals quotient. This yields realizationIso_exists without unproved data. A choice from this proved Nonempty theorem defines a realization isomorphism.

Compose localAdjunction with the proved ordinary tensor/restriction scalarAdjunction. Transport its left functor across realizationIso to obtain adjunction with the explicit R_n. This is rawAdjunction_exists, a proved Nonempty theorem. Define rawAdjunction by choice from that proved theorem; no reduction of its implementation is required when using its unit and counit.
